subject: SIG Questionnaire: telemetry, key-provenance & audit-log samples

From: Elaine Kwan <elaine.kwan@northbridge.com>

Cc: security@northbridge.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Northbridge SIG pick-up: runtime telemetry, key provenance, and audit log samples

Rohan —

Thanks for taking this on. Northbridge is running a SIG assessment this quarter and our security team flagged three areas where we need concrete artifacts and clarifications to advance your profile: (1) runtime telemetry and sampling strategy for inference requests, (2) cryptographic key provenance (KMS/HSM usage, key rotation proof), and (3) representative audit-log exports showing end-to-end events for request authentication and admin actions.

Requests:
- A completed SIG mapping sheet at the control level (we attached a template in our previous email).
- Representative audit-log export (redacted) for a 24h window showing user auth events, model invocation, and admin key ops. JSONL preferred.
- A diagram and short note describing how keys are generated/stored/rotated (KMS provider, HSM if used, ephemeral keys for KV cache).
- Clarify cross-region retention behavior for telemetry and logs (we need to know whether you store telemetry outside the request region).

Deadline: our internal deadline is EOD Oct 13 to include materials in the SIG packet. If you can provide a delivery plan today that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Elaine Kwan
Senior Security Analyst
Northbridge Capital

[Attachment: NBB_SIG_Template_v2.xlsx]

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Northbridge SIG pick-up: runtime telemetry, key provenance, and audit log samples

Rohan —

Quick technical notes to include in the response (drafted for the mapping file):

- Telemetry sampling: We sample 100% of admin control-plane events and 5% of inference request telemetry by default (configurable per customer). Sampling is stratified by model, sequence length bucket, and request latency to preserve tail behavior. We’ll include examples in the mapping.

- Audit log schema: our audit logs include fields: timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, principal_type (api_key/user/role), action (model.invoke, model.load, admin.key_rotate, kms.encrypt), result (success/fail), src_ip, user_agent. The JSONL export will include a 24-hour window for a demo tenant with tenant_id REDACTED_NORTH.

- Key provenance: We use customer-managed keys for Private deployments and Redwood-managed KMS for hosted customers. Root keys are stored in AWS KMS (multi-region CMK) and HSM-backed keys are used for dedicated HSM customers. Keys are rotated annually by default and we store rotation metadata (key_id, rotated_at, previous_key_id, rotation_audit_reference). Ephemeral session keys are used for KV cache encryption per-request and are derived using the KDF tied to the tenant symmetric key.

- Retention/cross-region: By default telemetry is retained in the request region for 90 days; aggregated metrics may be replicated to a central analytics region for platform health (anonymized). For customers requiring region-only residency we can enable strict regional retention and disable replication.

I’ll assemble the audit-log sample and the key_provenance_diagram.png — tagging Marissa for evidence packaging.

-Aditya
Senior Systems Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Internal note: ensure we do not include full API keys in export; use redaction script v2.1]
